scopeReview: IMP-6.A.1:residential forms and low/medium/high intensity, cultural/technological influences, development cycles and infill. Definitions distinguish dwelling units, residents, gross/net area, height, occupancy and crowding rather than attach universal value judgments to density.
varietyReview: Four meaningful stimuli:unit/area accounts, original paired infill plan, changing housing mix and gross/net denominators. Checks compute20/50 units perha, preserve the unchanged edge, recalculate20%/46.7% apartments and100gross versus200/500net. Source/scale cases complete eleven.
repetitionReview: Separate housing-stock, spatial-infill, mix-share and land-denominator tasks; added application items test equal density with different forms, height/use and crowding. No city name/number-only clone of prior geography items; varied keys and all-option reasoning, difficulty uncalibrated.
referenceNote: Official scope checked. Every housing count, parcel, rule change and example is original/hypothetical. No actual rent, code threshold, construction recommendation or resident identity inferred; no new resources or independent human review.

questions.independentReview: Independently computed20 and50units/ha, ratioB/A2.5. Units and residential-only area explicitly supplied; no household-size or occupancy assumption. Different from farming input intensity:the task identifies residential stock density.

questions.correctOption: Infill development within an already developed urban area.
questions.independentReview: Checked paired identical-size urban-edge polygons and central-lot replacement, with existing north/south buildings retained. No boundary expansion or displacement of listed residents is asserted; the parcel was explicitly vacant.

questions.correctOption: It rises from 20% to about 46.7%, while the total number of dwelling units also increases.
questions.independentReview: Independently summed1000→1500 units; apartment shares.20 and.466666..., rounded46.7%. Counts are housing stock, not population or occupied households, and categories are mutually exclusive.

questions.correctOption: Both gross densities are 100 residents/hectare, but net residential densities are 200 for A and 500 for B.
questions.independentReview: Independently recomputed gross[100,100] andnet[200,500]. Residential areas are subsets of the10ha totals. No assumption of uniform distribution, public-space quality or an objective best density.

questions.correctOption: Building use, dwelling count, occupancy and site area differ; height alone does not count residents.
questions.independentReview: Avoided equating skyscrapers, crowding and residential density. No actual tower occupancy or universal height-to-person conversion invented.

questions.correctOption: They can enable more usable floors on a site, but costs, demand, regulation and design affect whether that capacity is used for housing.
questions.independentReview: Aligned technological capabilities in IMP-6.A.1 without engineering advice or a guaranteed affordability effect.

questions.correctOption: Different development periods, cultural practices and capabilities can leave layers of residential form.
questions.independentReview: No actual culture assigned a fixed architecture or income category. Described built-form evidence without turning it into individual demographic inference.

questions.correctOption: Different building arrangements can produce similar dwelling densities, while household sizes and lived conditions may still differ.
questions.independentReview: No numerical-only clone of the first comparison; this tests nonuniqueness of built form under an equal measured ratio.

questions.correctOption: Before/after use, dwelling and resident counts, relevant area, occupancy and the timing of redevelopment.
questions.independentReview: Evidence selection does not assume a specific policy effect or that all underused sites are vacant. Keeps this redevelopment case distinct from the explicitly vacant infill map.

questions.correctOption: Every dwelling is overcrowded and every household experiences the same conditions.
questions.independentReview: Separated people/hectare from people/room without a medical or legal overcrowding threshold. No density range labeled inherently good or bad.

questions.correctOption: Planning rules, land availability, transport, cultural preferences and development cycles can shape how residents and buildings occupy space.
questions.independentReview: Aligned cultural, technological and development-cycle scope; no specific contemporary city density or causal estimate invented.
